scope: Proposition 3.7 of the manuscript “Harmonic heights and the Artin K(pi,1) conjecture” (preprints/Harmonic-heights-and-the-Artin-K-pi-1-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 254 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 08da57cf59c88b26), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 16-17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each original color i, let Bi = Y α∈f {i} Bα, Di = Y α∈f {i} Dα. These products are independent of their order up to bimodule homotopy. The assignments σi 7→ Bi and σ−1 i 7→ Di define an action of the original Artin group by invertible bimodule homotopy classes. For x ∈ A write Bx for a representing complex, and write Fi = Bi ⊗Z − on left complexes. For every H ∈ C , right tensoring of labels, TH(Ps,X) = Ps,X⊗H, 16 is an additive functor on projectives that preserves path lengths and extends to their bounded homotopy category. It commutes naturally up to homotopy with the positive and inverse color twists, and hence with each Bx ⊗Z −. All the action identities above are bimodule chain homotopy equivalences, so they remain valid upon tensoring with finite complexes of modules that are not projective.
